description: A failable function passed to a component as a declared `on*` PROP is a callback value, not a DOM handler reference. `<Btn onSave=risky/>` where `Btn` calls `onSave()` inside a guarded handler (`onclick={ onSave() !{ | .Empty :> @r = 1 } }`) — the component handles the error. `<Show onSave=risky/>` where `Show` never uses the prop as a handler. Neither fires E-ERROR-002.
provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S441 "yes on references" (the rule covers event-handler references; a component prop is not one — S441 review B1)
rationale: §19.4.3 (S441) — the reference rule applies to an event-handler attribute whose value is a `!` function. A declared component prop named `on…` is handed to the component, which decides how the function is called; where the component wires it as a raw handler reference, the rule fires at the call site (handler-failable-reference-pos covers the direct forms).
